title: What the Colon Sends Back — Inulin Fermentation, Eudragit Colon-Targeted [1-13C]SCFAs, Systemic Availability (36% Acetate, 9% Propionate, 2% Butyrate) & FFAR2 8J24

teenKit.tldr: You aren't digesting your food alone—trillions of gut microbes take your breakfast first, fermenting it into short-chain fatty acids that run a massive underground economy inside your body.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding this hidden microbial supply chain rewrites how we view human metabolism, showing that our health is deeply controlled by the chemical signals our gut sends back to us.
keyTakeaways: Up to 97% of energy produced in the lower gut is consumed or processed by your microbiome before it ever reaches your main bloodstream.
Specialized bacteria like Bacteroides ovatus and Roseburia work in teams through cross-feeding to break down complex carbs like inulin into valuable fatty acids.
Only a fraction of these microbial currencies actually make it past the liver into systemic circulation—specifically about 36% of acetate, 9% of propionate, and 2% of butyrate.

vocab.meaning: A complex carbohydrate found in plants that humans can't digest on their own, serving as prime food for our gut microbes.
Small fat molecules produced when gut bacteria ferment fiber, acting as crucial chemical messengers and energy sources.
A process where one species of gut bacteria breaks down a nutrient and passes the byproduct to another species to finish the job.
The percentage of a nutrient or chemical that successfully escapes the gut and liver to circulate through the entire body.

quiz.question: According to the episode, what percentage of the energy produced in your lower gut is typically intercepted by your microbiome?
quiz.explanation: The episode reveals that up to 97% of lower gut energy is stripped and mined by microbes before reaching your general bloodstream.

quiz.question: What happens to acetate after it is produced by gut microbes and absorbed?
options: It has the highest systemic availability among SCFAs, with about 36% making it past the liver into circulation.
It is immediately destroyed and never leaves the colon.
It converts instantly into solid bone tissue.
It bypasses the liver entirely with 100% efficiency.
quiz.explanation: Isotope tracing shows that about 36% of acetate survives clearance to become systemically available in the body.

quiz.question: What is the primary role of Eudragit S100 capsules mentioned in the research context?
options: To dye the digestive tract bright neon colors
To deliver colon-targeted tracer compounds safely to the lower gut
To instantly cure all bacterial infections
To block all nutrient absorption completely
quiz.explanation: Eudragit capsules are engineered to survive the upper GI tract and release their contents precisely in the colon for targeted scientific tracing.
